description: A line consisting solely of `![[` + 26-char id + `]]` is a transclusion directive; elsewhere the sequence is inert text.
given: Source markdown with a directive on its own line and the same sequence inline.

expect.outcome: Only the standalone line parses as a directive; the inline occurrence stays inert text.
asserts: A directive is a line consisting solely of ![[ + 26-char id + ]].
Inline occurrences are inert text.
The id must be a canonical 26-char Crockford base32 id.

description: A directive-looking sequence inside a code span or code block is inert text, never a directive.
given: Markdown containing ![[id]] inside an inline code span and inside a fenced code block.

expect.outcome: Both occurrences render as literal text; no transclusion is created.
asserts: Code spans and code blocks suppress directive parsing.
No transclusion or mention is produced from code content.
The literal sequence is preserved verbatim.

description: A directive immediately followed, with no blank line, by a markdown blockquote is a partial transclusion; a blank line detaches it.
given: A directive directly above a blockquote, and a second directive separated from its blockquote by a blank line.

expect.outcome: The adjacent blockquote is a partial transclusion; the detached one is a full transclusion and the blockquote stands alone.
asserts: Immediacy with no blank line marks the partial form.
A blank line detaches the directive from the blockquote.
The selection is the blockquote's text content.

description: `![[id@vN]]` is reserved: publishers MUST reject it at publish and readers MUST tolerate it as an unknown construct.
given: Source markdown containing a versioned directive ![[id@v2]].

expect.outcome: Publishing errors; a reader that encounters it wire-side ignores it as unknown rather than failing.
asserts: Publishers reject ![[id@vN]] at publish time.
Readers tolerate a reserved construct as unknown.
The reserved form is never silently treated as a plain transclusion.

description: `[[id]]` is a plain internal link resolved at publish and rendered as an absolute anchor; it is silent on the wire.
given: Source markdown containing an inline [[id]] beside a reserved ![[id@v1]].

expect.outcome: The plain link resolves and renders as an absolute anchor with no wire construct; the reserved form is rejected.
asserts: Plain links render as absolute anchors to the item's page.
They produce no transclusion, provenance or mention.
An unresolvable plain link is a publish error.

description: A plain [[id]] link is silent on the wire: no provenance, no mention, no relation.
given: A thread whose prose links an item with [[id]] but does not transclude it.

expect.outcome: The published document has only the rendered anchor; no transclusions entry and no outbound mention are created.
asserts: No transclusions entry is produced for a plain link.
No Webmention is sent for a plain link.
Only a rendered anchor appears in content_html.

description: Directive resolution order: local-published first, else imported current or pin-retained, else publish error.
given: A directive whose id exists both locally (published) and among imported rows.

expect.outcome: The local-published snapshot is chosen and baked.
asserts: Local-published resolves before imported.
The chosen version is the then-current local snapshot.
Imported matches are not consulted when a local match exists.

description: With no local match, a directive resolves to the imported current version or a pin-retained snapshot.
given: A directive whose id exists only as an imported row (current) or as a pin-retained snapshot.

expect.outcome: The imported current/pin-retained snapshot is baked, never a live fetch.
asserts: Imported-current or pin-retained is the second resolution tier.
The snapshot is baked locally, not fetched.
Drafts and L0 rows are never resolved.

description: More than one imported match for a directive is a publish error (ambiguous).
given: A directive whose id matches two different imported origins.

expect.outcome: Publishing fails with an ambiguity error rather than picking one.
asserts: More than one imported match is an error.
The publisher never guesses between origins.
The error names the ambiguous id.

description: A directive that resolves nowhere is a publish error; drafts and L0 rows count as no match.
given: A directive whose id names only a draft or an L0 wrapper row.

expect.outcome: Publishing fails; the draft/L0 row is never baked into the published document.
asserts: Drafts are invisible to the protocol and never resolve.
L0 rows are never transclusion sources.
An unresolved directive is a hard publish error.

description: Baking: the local snapshot is baked (never live-fetched) as <blockquote class="blyg-transclusion" data-blyg-id data-blyg-version>, with data-blyg-origin only for remote sources.
given: A thread transcluding an own-origin source and a remote source.

expect.outcome: Both are baked as blyg-transclusion blockquotes; only the remote one carries data-blyg-origin.
asserts: The bake is a local snapshot, never a live fetch.
blyg-transclusion and its data-* attributes are permanent wire tokens.
data-blyg-origin appears only for remote sources.

description: A plain-web transclusion target gets an ordinary markdown blockquote (no selector, no blyg-transclusion) and may carry a frozen cited label.
given: A quote of a plain web page that is not a blyg item.

expect.outcome: The blockquote is ordinary markdown, with no blyg-transclusion class or selector; a cited label may be frozen onto it.
asserts: No blyg-transclusion class for a plain-web target.
No selector is produced.
A frozen cited label may accompany it.

description: Later edits, withdrawal or pinning of a source do not change a thread's baked snapshot; transclusions[].version is provenance and there is no auto-pin.
given: A published thread whose transcluded source is later edited, withdrawn, or pinned.

expect.outcome: The thread's baked content is unchanged; no pin is created automatically.
asserts: The baked snapshot is immutable against later source changes.
Publishing never depends on the network.
transclusions[].version is provenance; there is no auto-pin.

description: A thread MUST NOT transclude a local thread whose transitive local transclusion closure contains its own id.
given: A thread attempting to transclude another local thread that (transitively) transcludes back to it.

expect.outcome: Publishing fails on the local transclusion closure cycle.
asserts: The local transclusion closure is computed before publish.
A cycle back to the thread's own id is a publish error.
Remote transclusions do not participate in the local closure check.

description: Republishing re-resolves every directive to the then-current local snapshot; a source withdrawn and not pin-retained is a publish error on republish.
given: A draft of a thread whose previously transcluded source has since been withdrawn without a retained pin.

expect.outcome: Republish re-resolves all directives and fails on the missing source.
asserts: Every directive re-resolves against the then-current snapshots.
A withdrawn, non-retained source is a publish error.
A pin-retained snapshot would resolve successfully.

description: A generation source is not a transclusion: source references never appear in transclusions and never produce a blyg-transclusion blockquote.
given: A thread with a generated span listing an own-origin source in its generated array.

expect.outcome: The source appears only in generated[].sources; no transclusions entry or blockquote is produced for it.
asserts: generated[].sources never appear in transclusions.
No blyg-transclusion blockquote is produced for a source.
The generated span wraps only the machine-generated prose.

description: An id is permanent identity and forked_from lineage is immutable: no construct may add, retarget or clear it after creation.
given: A published fork, then an attempt to edit, retarget or clear forked_from in a later draft.

expect.outcome: The id never changes and the lineage is refused: it can neither be added, retargeted nor cleared after creation.
asserts: Ids are permanent across versions, withdrawal and return.
forked_from is immutable after creation.
The referenced version named by forked_from is pinned.

description: A fork copies the pinned document, not its composition: the blyg-transclusion class MUST NOT survive and inherited [[id]] links flatten to ordinary markdown links.
given: A fork of a pinned remote fragment whose prose contains a transclusion and an internal link.

expect.outcome: The fork's own content is the byte-exact source prose plus a flattened blockquote; no blyg-transclusion class survives.
asserts: The byte-exact pinned source prose is copied.
Inherited transclusions flatten to an ordinary markdown blockquote.
Publishers disclose spans they know are machine-generated.

description: Custody runs one hop per fork; nothing carries verification through a chain of forks.
given: A fork of a fork: A forked from B, and B itself was forked from a remote C.

expect.outcome: A's lineage names B's pinned version only; no transitive custody of C is claimed.
asserts: forked_from names exactly one pinned version.
Custody is one hop; it does not chain.
No construct carries a claim about the chain's origin.

description: A stub_of is either a blyg reference (origin REQUIRED) or a plain-web {url} target; either MAY carry cited.
given: A stub thread whose stub_of is the plain-web {url} shape.

expect.outcome: The {url} shape is accepted with an optional cited label; the blyg shape requires origin.
asserts: The plain-web shape is {url} with optional cited.
The blyg shape requires origin.
stub_of names exactly one target; other transclusions are quotes.

description: cited is self-asserted and frozen: it MUST NOT be presented as verified or current, and is never baked into content_html; importers retain it verbatim.
given: A stub whose stub_of carries a cited label frozen at creation time.

expect.outcome: The cited label is carried verbatim in the reference and never appears in content_html or as a verified claim.
asserts: cited requires retrieved and is self-asserted.
It MUST NOT be baked into content_html.
Importers retain it verbatim and never re-derive it.

description: Stubs and lineage add no feed vocabulary; a stub is a thread and appears as one; any prepended citation line is presentation only.
given: A blyg feed containing a stub thread and a fork.

expect.outcome: The feed has no stub/lineage elements; the stub appears as an ordinary thread entry and any citation line is outside content_html.
asserts: No blyg:* element is introduced for stubs or lineage.
A stub thread contributes an ordinary thread entry.
A prepended citation/lineage line is presentation, not content.

description: Withdrawal does not cascade: a thread keeps its snapshot, a stub of a withdrawn item stays published, and a withdrawn stub should re-send its mention once.
given: A source item withdrawn after being transcluded in a thread and stubbed by another blyg.

expect.outcome: Neither the thread nor the stub is withdrawn; a withdrawn stub re-sends its mention once so the receiver marks it gone.
asserts: Withdrawal does not cascade to transcluders.
A stub of a withdrawn item stays published.
A withdrawn stub re-sends its mention once.

description: A changelog note MUST NOT reproduce withheld (unpinned) prior content.
given: A multi-version item in which earlier versions are unpinned and withheld.

expect.outcome: Notes describe the event without quoting the withheld earlier content.
asserts: The changelog is metadata, never a diff or content.
A note never reproduces withheld unpinned content.
Only the latest version's content is served.

description: Media objects are immutable once published: a media URL always serves the same bytes, and media referenced by any pinned version is retained forever.
given: An item referencing media/x7f2.png in content_html and a media[] entry pointing at the same origin-relative URL.

expect.outcome: The media URL is treated as immutable; content_html uses the absolute URL while media[].url stays origin-relative; pinned documents carry no media array.
asserts: A media URL always serves the same bytes once published.
content_html uses absolute media URLs; media[].url stays origin-relative.
Media referenced by a pinned version is retained forever.

description: page SHOULD be stable for the life of the item; a publisher forced to move it SHOULD serve a redirect.
given: An item with a page value, and a publisher that must move the page for a deployment reason.

expect.outcome: The page URL stays stable; a forced move is accompanied by a redirect from the old URL.
asserts: page is stable for the life of the item.
A moved page serves a redirect.
A withdrawn item's page is 200 forever.

description: Items are titleless: readers MUST NOT extract a title from content, and any feed <title> MUST NOT be read back as an item field.
given: An item whose content_md begins with a markdown heading and a feed entry carrying a derived <title>.

expect.outcome: No title is extracted from the content, and the feed <title> is not stored back onto the item.
asserts: Items are titleless.
Readers MUST NOT derive a title from content.
A feed title is presentation and never an item field.

description: A fork's HTML page SHOULD show its lineage, linking the pinned version it names.
given: The fork F whose forked_from names the remote pinned fragment R1 v1.

expect.outcome: F's permalink page shows a lineage link to the named pinned version.
asserts: The lineage link points at the referenced pinned version.
Lineage is presentation, not part of content_html.
The link names the origin, id and version.

description: The renderer wraps each generated span as <span class="blyg-tk-gen"> or <div class="blyg-tk-gen">; the class name is a permanent wire token.
given: The thread T whose published content_html wraps its machine-generated prose in a blyg-tk-gen element.

expect.outcome: The generated span is wrapped exactly with the permanent blyg-tk-gen class.
asserts: The wrapper class is exactly blyg-tk-gen.
blyg-tk-gen is a permanent wire token.
The wrapper surrounds only the generated prose.

description: Optional pinned pages are gated exactly like the JSON and are not publish events: they MUST NOT appear in the feed or archive index and readers MUST NOT require them.
given: The optional pinned page f/{id}/v2/index.html beside the pinned JSON.

expect.outcome: The pinned page is not in the feed or index, is gated like the JSON, and is optional to readers.
asserts: Pinned pages never appear in the feed or archive index.
They are gated exactly like the pinned JSON.
Readers MUST NOT require pinned pages to exist.

description: The HTML feed page carries <link rel="blogroll"> and <link rel="webmention"> when the corresponding surfaces exist.
given: The sample blyg whose manifest advertises a blogroll and a webmention endpoint.

expect.outcome: The feed page carries the blogroll and webmention link elements; the endpoint is announced in a Link header where possible.
asserts: A rel=blogroll link is emitted when the blogroll is advertised.
A rel=webmention link is emitted when mentions are accepted.
The endpoint may also be announced in an HTTP Link header.

description: A client MAY display imported content publicly as curation with attribution and links, without any protocol surface; displayed copies follow spec 13.4 on withdrawal.
given: A studio that curates an imported item on a public page outside the blyg surface.

expect.outcome: The curation carries attribution and links, exposes no protocol surface, and is removed/updated on withdrawal per spec 13.4.
asserts: Curation is presentation outside the blyg surface.
Attribution and a link to the source are required.
A withdrawn source's displayed copy follows spec 13.4.
